sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: Candidate faithfully implements the required ship target, applicability conditions, canonical tank classes through nltl:hasComponent, ship-owned capacity and separation quantities, date boundary, units, datatypes, and comparison thresholds.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: Replace the invented xsd:string tank-type alternatives "oil_residue_tank" and "oily_bilge_water_holding_tank" with an approved canonical representation. The COMPLETE contract explicitly requires nltl:oilResidueTank and nltl:oilyBilgeWaterHoldingTank, but the candidate omits both and treats their aliases as controlled literals even though tankType has no declared controlled values. Preserve the prior canonical tank-type repair, but do not type the ship itself as nltl:oilResidueTank or nltl:oilyBilgeWaterHoldingTank. Select a tank through the supplied nltl:hasComponent path and apply those canonical classes to that component, while retaining constructionDate, shipCategory, individualTankCapacity, and tankOuterShellSeparation on the ship as required by their authoritative owners. Rewrite the bounded constraint to report a violation for each applicable A/B ship constructed on or after "2017-01-01"^^xsd:date that has a represented canonical tank and a decimal M3 capacity greater than 30 when no decimal M separation of at least 0.76 exists. The current outer FILTER NOT EXISTS is accidental-pass logic: one capacity at or below 30 or one compliant capacity can hide another capacity above 30, while absence of capacity incorrectly causes a violation even though this universal tank rule does not require tank existence. Remove unsupported maxCount cardinalities and use a direct typed date comparison rather than decomposing the date with YEAR/MONTH/DAY.

Candidate faithfully implements the required ship target, applicability conditions, canonical tank classes through nltl:hasComponent, ship-owned capacity and separation quantities, date boundary, units, datatypes, and comparison thresholds.
